projects.definition: Task execution has one explicit control authority and one explicit release-transition model, so every Task can be attached, recovered, signaled, and promoted safely when OS process identity, provider Invocation state, and telemetry disagree or are incomplete.

krs.text: For 30 consecutive days of local Task operation, every liveness, signal, recovery, and promotion decision is attributable to one documented authority and matches OS/provider disagreement probes; no Task is stranded by contradictory control records.

Across 30 consecutive days and at least three promotions with live or recoverable Tasks, each Task has exactly one authoritative process tree before and after promotion, with no duplicate progress, lost handoff, or ambiguous release ownership.

Forced missing or stale ProcessOwner, provider Invocation, trace, and Exec evidence produces the designed attach, restart, recovery, or fail-closed outcome in tests and dogfood, and never signals a process whose exact ownership cannot be proven.

items.name: Decide Task control and release ownership boundaries
items.description:
Resolve the remaining architecture fork before implementation.

Choose and justify both boundaries:

1. Authority: whether exact OS-verifiable ProcessOwner identity is the sole authority for Task liveness, signaling, recovery, and promotion, or provider Invocation state can authorize or veto any of those actions.
2. Releases: whether promotion stops and restarts the current Task process or permits adjacent releases to coexist, including the exact owner and handoff rule for each live process tree.

Inspect the current Task Run, Invocation, attach/resume, Ask handoff, absent-owner recovery, local promotion, and trace/Exec paths. Produce one scratch design that maps authoritative state, transitions, failure behavior, and the minimum durable provider-session metadata. State the rejected alternative and why.

Done when the design names one unambiguous signal and recovery authority, specifies promotion behavior across the current and next binaries, identifies behavior under missing Invocation/trace/Exec evidence, and lists the focused behavioral proofs implementation must satisfy. Do not implement the control-path change in this Task.
